Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 14:03:00 -0400
Subject: Overrun relief request — May launch

Hi Jordan,

Quick note — our May feature launch drove significantly higher inference volume than our forecast, and we received an overrun invoice that will materially impact our month close. I attached a compact usage export for May (Altis_usage_May.csv).

We love Redwood’s latency and the team was great, but this spike was unexpected and exceeds our short-term budget for this quarter. Is there any discretionary relief you can provide for the overrun charges, or a short-term quota uplift while we finalize our capacity commit?

If helpful, we can join a quick call to go over numbers. Appreciate any flexibility — we’re evaluating a 3-month pilot commit to stabilize usage after launch, but need help with this first invoice to keep the program green internally.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Product
Altis AI

Attachments: Altis_usage_May.csv (CSV, 48KB)
From: jordan_blake@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Overrun relief request — May launch

Hi Samira — thanks for the note and for sharing the export. I pulled it in and can see the peak on May 12–14 that looks like the launch window. We want you to be successful here.

Two immediate options we can consider:
- One-time credit on the May overrun (we’ll need to confirm amounts with finance).
- Temporary quota uplift for July while we lock in a short-term commit (3 months) so you don’t hit hard limits during stabilization.

Before I propose specifics I’ll run this by finance and ops — can you share who in procurement we should loop for contract amendments? I see procurement@altis.ai cc’d, so that works.

I’ll follow up tomorrow with a concrete concession proposal and next steps (and I’ll attach a short proposal PDF).

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Overrun relief request — May launch

Folks — forwarding Altis’ note and the usage export. Key facts: May overrun driven by a single launch spike; they’re open to a 3-month pilot commit to stabilize (potential upsell).

Ask: can we do a one-time concession to preserve the account? Proposed starting point: 50% credit on the overrun invoice plus a temporary quota uplift for July (no additional charge) if they sign a 3-month pilot commit within 10 business days. If finance needs a smaller credit, we can offer 30% + a 10% discount on incremental usage for the first 3 months of the commit.

Reasoning: high retention potential; low long-term revenue risk if we trade a small credit for a committed runway.

Attached: Altis_usage_May.csv (from customer). I’ll draft a proposal PDF if you greenlight a concession range.

-J

Thanks for the context. A few quick items I need to evaluate:
1) Exact overrun dollar amount (run the May usage delta vs. their committed MU); can you paste the invoice line or estimated charge?
2) ARR/expected revenue if they convert to a 3-month pilot commit (and conversion probability).
3) Any precedent concessions for launch spikes for similar customers (we should be consistent).

From a finance POV, 50% credit is aggressive for an initial ask. I’m comfortable with a 25–35% one-time credit while structuring upside (e.g., 10% discount on incremental usage for three months and a firm monthly minimum for the pilot). If the estimated revenue from the pilot covers the credit within 90 days, escalate to 40% credit.

Can you run the simple calc and share the overrun estimate? I’ll model scenarios and pull precedence.

—Ben
Head of Revenue Operations

Attachments: (please attach the quick overrun calc spreadsheet when you reply)

Subject: Overrun relief proposal and next steps

Hi Samira / procurement team — thanks again for the export and for the patience while we reviewed internally.

Proposal (aimed at keeping you live and giving you runway to finalize a short-term commit):
1) One-time credit: 30% credit applied to the May overrun invoice. This is intended to materially reduce your immediate bill while preserving predictability.
2) Temporary uplift: We’ll raise your quota by 1.5x for the month of July at no additional charge to avoid throttling while you stabilize.
3) Pilot commit path: If Altis signs a 3-month pilot amendment (covering July–September) within 10 business days, you’ll receive a 10% discount on incremental usage above your current baseline for the first three months of that pilot. The amendment will also include a nominal monthly minimum to prevent repeated overrun exposure.

Attachments: redwood-proposal-v3.pdf (proposal + amendment draft), Altis_usage_May.csv (their export).
DocuSign (proposal & amendment): https://www.docusign.com/ndf?token=ALTIS-009-2026
